text:
Asha: taking handoff for 02:00-10:00 PT. Active incident: Redis throttling affecting embedding ingestion. Pager fired 01:14 UTC. Root cause suspected: connection saturation + large scan-heavy keys on hot slots. Current customer impact: elevated 95th/99th gen latency for ingestion and occasional 5xxs.

IncidentBot: ALERT -> redis-high-latency (us-west-2) triggered at 01:12 UTC. 3x baseline RPS, avg latency 120ms -> 800ms, command timeouts increasing.

Miguel: I saw the same. I've bumped consumer replicas from 8 -> 24 (k8s HPA spike) and rolled a consumer image with `redis-backoff=true` to reduce retry storms. Patch applied at 01:28 UTC.

Samir: confirmed scale applied. Watching queue length drop now (consumer_queue_length -> 22k -> 9k after 10m). Redis connected clients still high (~4800). I've applied `client-output-buffer-limit` tweak per runbook to protect primary.

Leah: customer-facing note: Two enterprise customers (acme-inc, beta-corp) reported slower ingestion. I've opened support tickets and flagged for prioritization. No data loss reported, only delays and 429s intermittently.

Asha: Mitigations in progress summarised: 1) consumer scale-up (done) 2) enable consumer-side backpressure + retry jitter (done) 3) temporary per-tenant ingress throttle at edge: set to 50req/s per API key for high-volume tenants (applied 01:35 UTC) 4) in-flight eviction policy on Redis: LRU priority on big keys (in review with infra team).

OpsBot: Runbook reminder: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/redis-throttling. Relevant playbook steps: `kubectl -n inference scale deploy/consumer --replicas=24`, `redis-cli CONFIG SET client-output-buffer-limit 0 0 0`, and `edgectl rate-limit update --key <tenant> --rps 50`.

Samir: quick logs snippet showing retry storms (01:10-01:20 UTC):
```
[01:12:03] consumer-3 WARN retrying msg id=... after 500ms
[01:12:07] consumer-7 ERROR redis timeout cmd=GET key=embed_cache:large_list
[01:13:40] consumer-12 INFO backoff applied delay=1200ms
```

Miguel: Note — we observed a couple of large keys (multi-MB) being scanned by a batch job. I've temporarily disabled that batch job in prod, queued a fix to iterate with `SCAN` chunks instead of `KEYS`. Job disabled at 01:30 UTC.

Asha: What to watch during my shift: `redis_command_latency_p95`, `redis_connected_clients`, `consumer_queue_length`, `ingest_5xx_rate`, `edge_rate_limited_count`. Alerts to act on: redis_high_latency (sev2), consumer_queue_backlog (sev3), edge_rate_limit_spike (informational).

Leah: Coverage note: secondary for next 2 hours is unassigned — @Miguel can you be backup until 04:00 PT? We should avoid gap while we validate the eviction policy change.

Miguel: ack, I'll be secondary until 04:00 PT. I'll also keep a closer eye on the infra logs for large key scans.

Asha: temporary owner for runbook edits: Samir — please add the `client-output-buffer-limit` and `large-key-scan` steps we used into the runbook with exact commands and the rollback steps.

Samir: on it. I'll update the runbook and push a short changelog in the doc at 02:05 PT.

OpsBot: Note: Pager escalation policy still enabled. If redis_high_latency remains >7min, auto-escalate to SRE lead.

Asha: Handoff checklist for incoming oncall: - current state: mitigations applied, ingestion latency trending down but not back to baseline - outstanding actions: runbook update (Samir), eviction policy rollout (pending infra review), confirm per-tenant throttle effects after 1hr - visible impact: elevated latency for few customers, no data loss - point of contact: me (Asha) primary, Miguel secondary until 04:00 PT.

Leah: Added note for post-mortem if incident persists beyond recovery window: capture batch job causing KEYS usage, timeline of scaling, and customer impact timeline.

Asha: I'll stay on the thread for another 45m to monitor and will escalate if anything regresses. Please react with :thumbsup: to acknowledge coverage.

Miguel: :thumbsup:

Samir: :thumbsup:

Leah: :thumbsup:

IncidentBot: Incident status: ongoing -> mitigation in progress. Next automated check 02:10 PT.

Asha: end of handoff message.
